title: The macro that ate my message
prompt:
This program reads a ticket count and a price in cents, multiplies them, and prints the bill on one line. With the input `3 125` it should print:

```
count = 3, price = 125, total = 375
```

Run it and read what it prints instead. The multiply is fine; the words in the message are what went wrong.

m4 reads the whole file before the assembler does, and it replaces every whole word that matches a `define` name, even inside a quoted string. Fix the program so the message prints exactly as shown above, without changing the text between the quotes.

## what is checked

- with the input `3 125` the bill line matches word for word
- the program returns 0
- the checker also runs a few inputs you do not see, including a count of zero, a negative price, and a total too big for 32 bits
starter:
// read a ticket count and a price in cents, then print the bill
// on one line

define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(count, x19)
define(price, x20)
define(total, x21)

.data
fmt_in:     .string "%ld %ld"
fmt_out:    .string "count = %ld, price = %ld, total = %ld\n"

.bss
.balign 8
count_m:    .skip 8
price_m:    .skip 8

.text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // scanf fills both slots
        ldr     x1, =count_m
        ldr     x2, =price_m
        bl      scanf

        ldr     x9, =count_m
        ldr     count, [x9]
        ldr     x9, =price_m
        ldr     price, [x9]
        mul     total, count, price         // the bill, in cents

        ldr     x0, =fmt_out
        mov     x1, count
        mov     x2, price
        mov     x3, total
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
